rule: Column moments: the camera is on the marked column 0.3 s before the sentence; the change starts moving 1.5 s after the sentence appears (1.6 s), ends >= 0.5 s before it ends; then >= 1.5 s still with an empty band. A without a move: >= 2 s watch. D: its subject on screen >= 0.55 s before. Each sentence max(3 s, words/1.8 + 1.0 s).

moments.text:
Five rows, one per model.
Every row plays the same small change: rename a field that other teams read.
Every model starts from a written intent.
Then each one writes requirements, or a spec.
Watch the purple boxes. That is where the architecture rule lives.
In every model, the rule is something the agent reads.
The work is broken into tasks.
The agent writes the code. In every row, the old name is gone.
Review. Where a model has one, it is advice. It does not block.
Now CI. Only the last row has an architecture check.
Red. Rule ARCH-4 blocks the merge.
The agent fixes the code, and CI passes.
Release: a person says yes. The other teams keep working.
The rule is written down in every model.
The real question: does a check run after the code?
